title: Borrow Checker Internals
concept: The borrow checker enforces XIOM's ownership rules at compile time — preventing use-after-move, data races, and aliasing violations without runtime cost.
why: The borrow checker is XIOM's defining feature. Understanding its algorithms explains why some programs compile and others don't, and how to write checker-friendly code.
tips: The borrow checker works on CONTROL FLOW GRAPH, not text order — it understands if/else and loops
Non-Lexical Lifetimes (NLL) mean borrows end after last USE, not at end of scope — more code compiles
Use `clone()` to get independent copies instead of fighting the borrow checker
Split code into smaller functions — borrow checker analysis is per-function
common_mistakes: Fighting the borrow checker instead of restructuring code — sometimes clone() is the right answer
Keeping borrows alive too long — use scoped blocks `{ let r = &x; use(r); }` to limit borrow scope
Borrowing in loop bodies where mutable access is also needed — extract the borrow outside the loop
